original_question: A 57-year-old patient with a past medical history of alcoholism presents to the emergency room vomiting bright red blood. Vital signs are temperature 37 degrees Celsius, heart rate 141 beats per minute, blood pressure 90/60, respiratory rate 20, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. In the endoscopy suite, the patient also receives IV octreotide. After intervention and resolution of the acute bleed, which of the following pharmacologic agents is indicated?

original_question: A 66-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room due to abdominal distension and persistent somnolence for the past 2 weeks. On physical examination, the patient is altered and not responsive to commands, oriented x 0. The abdomen is significantly distended. Shifting dullness is present and a positive fluid wave can be elicited. Hyperreflexia and asterixis are noted. Laboratory findings are significant for the following: Laboratory test Sodium 140 mEq/L Potassium 3.5 mEq/L Chloride 97 mEq/L Glucose 90 mg/dL Ammonia 100 µg/dL (ref: 19-60 µg/dL) Arterial blood gas pH 7.4 pCO2 40 mm Hg pO2 90 mm Hg HCO3 26 mEq/L An abdominal ultrasound shows surface nodularity compatible with cirrhosis but no other changes aside from ascites. An upper GI endoscopy is performed which shows gastric varices with no signs of active bleeding. An MRI of the brain is insignificant. What is the most likely precipitating factor that led to this patient's condition?
final_question_original: What is the most likely precipitating factor that led to this patient's condition?
final_question_expected: What is the most likely precipitating factor that led to this patient's condition?
options: {"A": "Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis", "B": "Metabolic alkalosis", "C": "Portal vein thrombosis", "D": "Hypoglycemia"}

original_question: A 47-year-old patient comes to the physician because of progressive muscle weakness for five months. They feel that the muscles in their shoulders and hips have been getting weaker and sometimes feel sore. They now have difficulty getting up from chairs, climbing stairs, and combing their hair. The patient has also noticed new difficulty with swallowing solid foods, but has no trouble with liquids. They have a 5-year history of hyperlipidemia controlled with fluvastatin. A maternal uncle died at age 26 from Duchenne's muscular dystrophy and the patient's mother has Hashimoto's thyroiditis. Vital signs are within normal limits. Neurologic examination shows moderate weakness in the arm abductors and hip flexors bilaterally. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 13.7 g/dL Leukocytes 11,200/mm3 Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 33 mm/h Serum Creatine kinase 212 U/L Lactate dehydrogenase 164 U/L AST 34 U/L ALT 35 U/L Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

Current medications include amitriptyline and diphenhydramine. The patient does not respond to questions and repeatedly says, "The government is following me everywhere." The temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 115/min, respirations are 24/min, and blood pressure is 160/89 mm Hg. The patient is diaphoretic. The patient is not oriented to place or time. After the examination, the patient starts screaming and tries to bite the physician. Urine toxicology screening is positive for ethyl glucuronide. They say that the pain “comes and goes” throughout the day and usually lasts 20-30 minutes per episode. They can point to the spot 1-2 inches above the umbilicus where they feel the pain. They deny any feeling of regurgitation or nighttime cough but endorse nausea. They report that they used to eat three large meals per day but have found that eating more frequently improves their pain. They tried a couple pills of ibuprofen with food over the past couple days and think it helped. They have gained four pounds since their past appointment three months ago. The patient denies any diarrhea or change in their stools. They have no past medical history. They drink 5-6 beers on the weekend and have a 20 pack-year smoking history. They deny any family history of cancer. On physical exam, they are tender to palpation above the umbilicus. Bowel sounds are present. A stool guaiac test is positive. The patient undergoes endoscopy with biopsy to diagnose their condition. Which of the following is most likely to be found on histology?
final_question_original: Which of the following is most likely to be found on histology?
final_question_expected: Which of the following is most likely to be found on histology?
options: {"A": "Mucosal defect in the stomach", "B": "Urease-producing organism in the small intestine", "C": "PAS-positive material in the small intestine", "D": "Crypt abscesses in the large intestine"}
reference_answer: Urease-producing organism in the small intestine

A noncontrast CT of the head shows a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). The patient is taken to the operating room, where the SAH is evacuated, and the vessel is repaired. Postoperatively, the patient is unresponsive. Several days later, a repeat CT of the head shows an enlarging aneurysm in a different vessel in the brain. The patient's child is asked to consent to a non-emergent, life-saving operation since the patient is in a comatose state. They do not consent to the operation even though the physician stresses it would be life-saving. Upon further discussion, the physician finds out that the patient was abusive and neglectful to their children, and the child wants “to live in peace.” The patient has no written advanced directive. Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?
final_question_original: Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?
final_question_expected: Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?
options: {"A": "Follow the daughter’s wishes to withhold the operation", "B": "Refer this case to the court", "C": "Contact another family member for consent", "D": "Report the daughter to the police"}
reference_answer: Contact another family member for consent

The nurse who evaluated the patient tried to stand them up, but when the patient tried to stand on the right leg, they dropped the left hip and lost balance. The nurse then recognized that the patient had a foreshortened right leg fixed in the adducted position and a large swelling in the right buttock. At the receiving hospital, the patient was confused and, though they knew their name, couldn’t remember the date and insisted on leaving the hospital immediately to see family. Past medical history includes diabetes, congestive heart failure, and incontinence. The patient is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, metoprolol, and oxybutynin. Physical exam confirmed the nurse’s findings. Radiographs proved the presence of a right posterior hip dislocation without fractures. What medication is most likely associated with this patient’s confusion?

Their mood has been stable on the current dose of citalopram. They take ibuprofen for headaches but previously borrowed a friend’s headache medication when the headaches became very severe. Of note, the patient has been trying to lose weight and recently started taking an amino acid supplement at the suggestion of a relative who is a nutritionist. They are also trying out a new low-carbohydrate diet. The patient works as a nurse at a local primary care clinic. Their temperature is 101.5°F (38.6°C), blood pressure is 144/80 mmHg, pulse is 108/min, and respirations are 22/min. They are diaphoretic and shivering. Patellar and brachioradialis reflexes are 3+ bilaterally. Tone is increased in their bilateral upper and lower extremities. Rapid dorsiflexion of their right ankle elicits 3 beats of clonus. Pupils are equally round and reactive to light. A basic metabolic panel is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely inciting factor for this patient’s condition?
final_question_original: Which of the following is the most likely inciting factor for this patient’s condition?
final_question_expected: Which of the following is the most likely inciting factor for this patient’s condition?

The patient has been unable to recall the family member's name or their address. There has been insomnia and daytime sleepiness during this period. The last bowel movement was 3 days ago. One month ago, the patient underwent a transjugular intrahepatic portal shunt (TIPS) placement. The patient has alcoholic liver cirrhosis. Current medications include spironolactone and furosemide. The patient used to drink over a pint of vodka daily but quit 2 months ago. They are oriented to place and person. The temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 88/min, and blood pressure is 102/64 mm Hg. Examination shows scleral icterus and jaundice. There are several telangiectasias over the chest and back. Palmar erythema is present. The abdomen is mildly distended and nontender. Shifting dullness is present. There is a flapping tremor of both hands when outstretched and dorsiflexed. Neurologic examination shows no other focal findings. The patient completes the number connection test slower than the age-normalized standard. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

final_question_expected: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

Examination of the left knee shows tenderness on palpation of the anteromedial joint line; there is crepitus and pain with full flexion and extension. final_question_original: Which of the following is the most likely finding on imaging of the left knee?
final_question_expected: Which of the following is the most likely finding on imaging of the left knee?
options: {"A": "Osteophytes with joint-space narrowing on x-ray", "B": "Diffuse lytic-sclerotic bone lesions on x-ray", "C": "Joint effusion and pannus on ultrasound", "D": "Fluid-filled pouch on ultrasound"}
reference_answer: Osteophytes with joint-space narrowing on x-ray

original_question: A 52-year-old patient presents to the clinic with a headache and dizziness for the past month. The patient reports that about 4 weeks ago, they developed a “nagging” headache. They thought they had a cold, so they tried over-the-counter ibuprofen that provided only mild and temporary relief. Recently, the patient also started feeling dizzy and nauseous, which only resolves when stepping outside to shovel the snow. The patient’s medical history is significant for hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and asthma. Their medications include amlodipine, metformin, glimepiride, and a fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler. The patient has been living at their upstate cabin for the past 5 weeks but denies other recent travel. They deny smoking tobacco or illicit drug use. The patient’s temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 130/78 mmHg, pulse is 72/min, and respirations are 16/min with an oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. The patient is currently asymptomatic while sitting in the office, and physical examination is unremarkable. Labs are drawn, as shown below: Hemoglobin: 20 g/dL Hematocrit: 60% Leukocyte count: 10,050 cells/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 350,000/mm^3 Which of the following underlies the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

Over the past 3 years, the patient has been dressing all in black and wears a long black coat, even in the summer. The mother reports that her child has always had difficulties fitting in. They do not have any friends and spend most of their time in their room playing online games. The patient is anxious at college because they are uncomfortable around other people, and their academic performance is poor. Rather than doing their coursework, they spend most of their time reading up on paranormal phenomena, especially demons. They say that they have never seen any demons, but sometimes there are signs of their presence. For example, a breeze in an enclosed room is likely the “breath of a demon.” Mental status examination shows laborious speech. The patient avoids eye contact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
final_question_original: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
